account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: correspondence, market walk, lunch, town accounts, tea with my neighbour, and afternoon office business. I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury. The appointments chest was empty after I had earlier seen the secretary remove the appointment book; I do not know any unusual reason for that. The secretary has been coordinating my appointments, including confirming the location of tea directly with my neighbour.

Several townspeople reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn and near the plaza. I also saw freight give the baker an emerald. These could simply be ordinary bread sales or deliveries; I have no evidence of anything improper. My neighbour likewise thought carrying bread natural for a baker.

At tea my neighbour mentioned vague, unverified talk of a bridge or port change. I asked about it at the office. The builder says no bridge or port works are proposed by them, which does not establish whether anyone else has plans.

The concrete new business is the builder's request for a brief inspection inside the great hall tomorrow, day one, at eighteen sharp. The builder says eight lanterns are installed. The secretary checked that the time was available before my nineteen-o'clock return home. I have agreed aloud and asked the secretary to record it, although both have since asked for confirmation again. Their requests may simply have overlapped with my reply. As far as I know, the inspection is to review the hall lighting; I have seen no evidence of another purpose.
